Faralei walks on to the center of the stage, then gives a smirk as she claps her hands together and every light on the stage shuts off. Violin music begins to play.

She pulls her hands out and a small bead of light forms between them. It raises up higher, growing and growing. Then it splits into many little pieces, like glass scattered in the air. 

The light scatters above the crowd as well, some lights shifting blue and red and pink and purple. Whether if it’s reflecting light or by design, no one knows. 

As the music crescendos, the lights twirl and twirl, the speed increasing, until they all blur together in a dizzying dance of the colors of the rainbow.  Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Violet— and a little pink, too. As the music hits its final note, the light bursts, and little drops of sunlight fall to the ground.
